newsitem.title: USA: MCN boosts production from Wyoming field.
newsitem.headline: MCN boosts production from Wyoming field.

text.p: MCN Energy Group Inc said Tuesday its MCNIC Oil & Gas Co unit is continuing to record drilling successes in the rapidly developing Jonah field in Sublette County, Wyoming.
The Jonah Federal 3-4 well has been brought onto production, averaging 10.7 million cubic feet per day of natural gas and 163 barrels per day of condensate during the first seven days, MCN said.
The well, drilled to a depth of 10,349 feet, was completed in the middle and upper Lance formation of the field.

MCNIC Oil & Gas purchased a one-third working interest in a 52,000-acre block in and around the Jonah field in May 1996, at which time the field was producing 16 million cubic feet of gas per day from 12 wells. Currently, gross production from the field is about 95 million cubic feet per day from 32 wells.

Included in the purchase last year was a one-third interest in a 40-mile gathering system, which has undergone a series of expansions to increase its capacity from 42 million cubic feet per day to 120 million.

"Results at Jonah have greatly exceeded our expectations in terms of profitability, deliverability and reserves," said Rai Bhargava, president and CEO of MCN Investment Corp, parent of MCNIC Oil & Gas. "We have high hopes for further expansion of this field, including the pipeline infrastructure."

More than 30 additional proven, undeveloped locations have been identified and are ready to drill in the Jonah field, MCN said. Proven reserves associated with the field at the end of 1996, net to MCNIC Oil & Gas, were 63 billion cubic feet equivalent of natural gas.
MCNIC's partner in the field, McMurry Oil Co, serves as operator. McMurry is a privately held company based in Casper, Wyo.
